title: Can you reach each number in two different ways?
description: A question from the book asks for at least two different button ways to make five numbers with Creative Chitti. The video trades a bigger press for ten smaller presses to find a second way for each number, and checks every second way by adding the parts.
teaching_notes: One idea: a bigger press can be traded for ten presses of the button below, so every number has many ways, and every way must add back to the number. Ask the class to add the parts of each way before accepting it. Watch for students who trade one press for fewer or more than ten presses.

source: Figure it Out (many ways with Chitti)
video_script.why: The child has traded a thousand for ten hundreds to find a different way to make 5072.
video_script.substitution: A bigger press is traded for ten presses of the button below, and every way must add back to the number.
video_script.anchor: Write at least two different ways for each of five numbers, from 8300 to 367813, as Creative Chitti would
video_script.payoff_line: Every way adds back to its number

final_answer.value: Each number has many ways; two ways for each are shown, and every expression adds to its number
final_answer.spoken: every way adds back to its number

maths_rules: check: each second way adds back to its number

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to write two different ways for each number, as expressions.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take eight thousand three hundred. Way one is eight thousands and three hundreds.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Way two trades three thousands for thirty hundreds, giving five thousands and thirty three hundreds.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Next, forty thousand six hundred twenty nine. Way one is forty thousands, six hundreds, two tens and nine ones.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Way two trades ten thousands for hundreds, and the tens for ones. That gives thirty thousands, one hundred six hundreds, and twenty nine ones.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, take fifty six thousand three hundred fifty four. Way one is fifty six thousands, three hundreds, five tens, and four ones.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Way two trades ten thousands for hundreds, and the tens for ones. That gives forty six thousands, one hundred three hundreds, and fifty four ones.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Next, sixty six thousand six hundred sixty six. Way one is sixty six thousands, six hundreds, and sixty six ones.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Way two uses every place once: six ten thousands, six thousands, six hundreds, six tens, and six ones.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, take three lakh sixty seven thousand eight hundred thirteen. Way one is three lakhs, six ten thousands, seven thousands, eight hundreds, one ten, and three ones.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Way two trades the three lakhs for thirty ten thousands, making thirty six ten thousands in all. The rest stays the same.

marks.m1: the sums for 8300 and 40629 are written
marks.m2: the sums for 56354 and 66666 are written
marks.m3: the sum for 367813 is written and a tick appears beside each

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check by adding the parts of each second way. Five thousand and three thousand three hundred make eight thousand three hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty thousand, ten thousand six hundred, and twenty nine make forty thousand six hundred twenty nine. The next two sums return their numbers too.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Add three lakh sixty thousand, seven thousand, eight hundred, ten, and three. It returns three lakh sixty seven thousand eight hundred thirteen.
